مَغْلُولٌ , applied to a man, Having the [shackle called] غُلّ put upon him. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [v. 69], وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ يَدٌ ٱللّٰهِ مَغْلُولَةٌ [And the Jews said, The hand of God is shackled], meaning, withheld from dispensing. (O.) ＝
-A2- Also, (S, K,) applied to a man, (S,) and ↓ غَلِيلٌ , and ↓ مُغْتَلٌّ , (K,) Thirsty; or vehemently thirsty; (K, TA;) or affected with burning of thirst, (S, TA,) little or much; (TA;) or with burning of the inside, (K, TA,) from thirst, or from anger and vexation. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
